newsitem.title: FRANCE: Three ETA French commandos jailed for life.
newsitem.headline: Three ETA French commandos jailed for life.

text.p: A special French court on Thursday gave life sentences to three suspected members of the ETA Basque separatist group's notorious "French commando" after finding them guilty of guerrilla attacks in Spain between 1978 and 1989.
Given life prison terms for the series of attacks in which 37 people died were Jean Parot, 46, Jacques Esnal, 46, and Frederic Haramboure, 43.

Separately, a second French court jailed three former ETA leaders for 10 years, the maximum sentence they faced on charges of terrorist conspiracy. ETA is believed to have killed some 800 people in its three-decade-old campaign for a Basque state independent from Madrid.

The second court jailed Spaniards Francisco "Pakito" Mugica Garmendia, the former operational commander of ETA, as well as explosives expert Jose Maria "Fiti" Arregui Erostarbe and ideologist Jose Luis "Txelis" Alvarez Santa Cristina.

It also jailed for 10 years Frenchman Pierre Fagant, 59, convicted of harbouring -- in the basement of his home in the southwestern French Basque region -- a clandestine ETA arms workshop producing hundreds of sub-machineguns a year.
The court handed down lesser jail sentences against most of some 20 other Spanish and French defendants on charges of aiding and abetting the guerrillas.

The three ETA leaders were captured five years ago in a hideout in the French Basque region. They have been previously condemned in France on other charges, and courts have authorised their extradition to Spain once they complete serving their sentences.
Mugica Garmendia, 43, was among the most wanted men in Spain, where he is accused of sending a booby-trapped car to Madrid in 1991 and has been described by police as the ETA's operational chief.

Santa Cristina, 42, was accused of being the ETA's ideologist and financier, in charge of extorting "revolutionary taxes" from businessmen in the Spanish Basque country, while 50-year-old Arregui Erostarbe, was said to be the group's expert on explosives and forged identity documents.
He is wanted in Spain in connection with a parcel bomb which in 1990 badly maimed Fernando de Mateo Lage, presiding judge of the Audiencia Nacional anti-terrorist court.

The French commando, ETA's only squad made up of non-Spaniards, was smashed after its presumed leader, Henri Parot, was arrested in 1990 as he drove a car loaded with 323 kilos of explosives into Seville which was then preparing to host the 1992 World Fair.

Spanish police believe the explosives were intended to blow up the city's police headquarters. Parot is being held in Spain and Spanish authorities had turned down a request from the Paris court to summon him as a witness.

Police hold the commando unit responsible for the deaths of 10 senior Spanish army and navy officers, two magistrates, a businessman who refused to pay ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) "revolutionary taxes" and several passers-by.
In its bloodiest attack, the squad bombed a Civil Guard barracks in Saragossa in 1987, killing 11 people, including children, and wounding 78.

Three other suspected commando members on trial in the special court got lesser prison terms. Jean-Pierre Erremundeguy, 42, was sentenced to six years in jail while Jean-Vincent Garcia, 42, and Philippe Saez, a 38-year-old monk, were given 10-year terms.
